title: Collision probability bound for random hashing
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $k \ge 1$, so that each hash value lies in $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$. Consider the space of hash functions $h \colon \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, equipped with the uniform product probability measure, and fix two distinct points $x \ne y$ in $\alpha$. Then the probability that $x$ and $y$ collide is at most $1/k$:
\[
  \Pr\bigl[\,h(x) = h(y)\,\bigr] \;\le\; \frac{1}{k}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: x and y are distinct (x ≠ y)
h ranges over the space of hash functions α → Fin k under the uniform product measure
replaced:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, $k \ge 1$, and let $x \ne y \in \alpha$.
For a uniformly random hash function $h : \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$,
\[
  \Pr[h(x) = h(y)] \;\le\; \frac{1}{k}.
\]
That is, $\mu_{\mathbb{R}}\bigl(\{h \in \texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k \mid h(x) = h(y)\}\bigr) \le 1/k$.
